definitions.explanation: The first part of autumn, roughly corresponding to September in Japan. Often still warm, with the first hints of cooler weather.

examples.japanese: {初秋|しょしゅう}の{風|かぜ}が{心地|ここち}よい。
examples.english: The early autumn breeze is pleasant.

examples.japanese: {初秋|しょしゅう}とはいえ、まだ{暑|あつ}い{日|ひ}が{続|つづ}く。
examples.english: Although it's early fall, the hot days continue.

examples.japanese: {初秋|しょしゅう}のころ、{空|そら}の{色|いろ}が{少|すこ}しずつ{変|か}わり{始|はじ}める。
examples.english: Around early autumn, the color of the sky begins to change little by little.

notes:
A literary and seasonal word used in writing, haiku, and weather reports. Part of a series of seasonal divisions: {初秋|しょしゅう} (early), {仲秋|ちゅうしゅう} (mid), {晩秋|ばんしゅう} (late autumn). The same pattern applies to other seasons.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {初秋|しょしゅう}の{風|かぜ}: early autumn breeze
- {初秋|しょしゅう}の{候|こう}: the early autumn season (epistolary)
- {初秋|しょしゅう}の{空|そら}: the early autumn sky

RELATED SEASONAL TERMS:
- {仲秋|ちゅうしゅう}: mid-autumn — the middle period, associated with the harvest moon
- {晩秋|ばんしゅう}: late autumn — the final stretch before winter
- {初夏|しょか}: early summer — the same pattern applied to summer
- {立秋|りっしゅう}: start of autumn — a specific date in the traditional calendar (around August 7)
